description:
Two correct-by-construction fixes uncovered while completing the runtime-demand cutover for the opaque joined-callable case (fixtures2/behavior/opaque_fn_value_join.fz). Both stand on their own merits; they make the previously-red native test green. The deeper boxed-return obligation (boxed first-class boundary target must present a boxed return) is tracked separately.

## Change
1. runtime_demand.rs `derive_callable_flow_facts_for_executable`: a `CallableFlowFact` now carries only most-specific surfaces (`retain_most_specific_surfaces`). When an escaped callable is observed at both a concrete surface and the polymorphic template it instantiates, the template surface is dropped — it would otherwise mint a phantom resolution that collapses onto its grounded sibling after type erasure and force an impossible boundary choice. A genuinely polymorphic escape (no concrete sibling) keeps its surface.
2. native.rs `settled_callable_boundary`: now a pure policy read of the value's CallableId boundary_ids (translated to native boundary ids), deleting the (function, capture_count, resolution) reverse-search. Native trusts transport's minted boundary policy; multiple boundaries here is a defensive error meaning the value should have arrived via a publication position.

## Check
`cargo test --lib` green (2216/0), zero warnings. The native test compiler2_native_program_joins_callable_resume_before_materializing_closure_call passes. Matrix opaque_fn_value_join remains red at AOT codegen (fault: boxed first-class boundary target return repr) — pre-existing, tracked under fz-rh2.29.
title: Opaque joined callable: drop phantom polymorphic surfaces and read native boundary policy
